jobs.title: Director, IT Applications
jobs.description:
Drive Technology Innovation and Build High-Performing Teams at Liberty Dental Plan

Are you a strategic technology leader who excels at developing people, partnering with the business, and delivering enterprise applications that drive measurable results? Liberty Dental Plan is seeking a Director, IT Applications
to lead a critical portfolio of business applications while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Reporting to the VP, Application Development
, this highly visible leadership role combines technology strategy, operational excellence, and people leadership. You will help shape the future of our application landscape, strengthen business partnerships, and guide a talented team responsible for delivering reliable, secure, and scalable solutions that support our members, clients, and organization.

About The Role

The Director, IT Applications is responsible for leading the delivery, support, maintenance, and ongoing evolution of enterprise applications across assigned business areas. This role ensures applications meet business needs, service level commitments, quality standards, and security requirements while supporting operational performance and organizational growth.

The ideal candidate brings a combination of healthcare payer industry knowledge, strong people leadership capabilities, business acumen, and experience managing vendor relationships and enterprise application portfolios.

Location:
Remote

Reporting Relationship:
VP, Application Development

What You'll Do

Technology Strategy & Application Leadership

Lead the delivery, support, maintenance, and optimization of critical business applications.
Serve as the product owner for assigned application platforms, establishing strategic priorities, modernization initiatives, and technology roadmaps.
Partner with business leaders to understand requirements, identify process bottlenecks, and recommend technology solutions that improve efficiency and productivity.
Balance business priorities, operational stability, modernization efforts, and technical debt reduction.
Guide application strategy and influence technical direction in partnership with technical teams and stakeholders.

Operational Excellence

Ensure applications meet agreed-upon service level expectations for availability, performance, incident response, and production support.
Oversee release planning, production readiness, ongoing maintenance, and enhancement activities.
Maintain strong controls around data integrity, compliance, security, and system management.
Monitor application health, technical debt, and remediation efforts while communicating risks and progress to leadership.
Identify and proactively address operational and delivery risks to ensure successful outcomes.
Support audits, client reviews, regulatory inquiries, proposal responses, and new client implementation activities.

Vendor & Stakeholder Management

Build and maintain strong relationships with vendors, business leaders, and cross-functional partners.
Manage third-party resources and consulting relationships to support delivery and operational objectives.
Partner with compliance, security, infrastructure, architecture, governance, and business operations teams to ensure alignment and execution.
Navigate competing priorities effectively while maintaining strong stakeholder relationships and transparency.

People & Team Leadership

Lead, coach, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of technology professionals.
Create an environment where employees feel supported, empowered, and accountable for results.
Establish clear expectations and provide ongoing performance feedback and development opportunities.
Foster collaboration, trust, continuous learning, and professional growth.
Delegate effectively while developing future leaders and building organizational capability.
Recognize and celebrate team contributions while maintaining a high-performance culture.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in IT applications, application support, systems delivery, or a related discipline.
5+ years of people leadership experience.
Strong understanding of application delivery, support, operations, and service level management.
Experience with software development lifecycles, release management, production support, and application maintenance practices.
Experience managing vendors, budgets, resources, operational risks, and delivery governance.
Ability to build trusted relationships with business leaders, technical teams, and external partners.
Strong communication, problem-solving, decision-making, and leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Healthcare payer experience, including Medicare and/or Medicaid environments.
Dental payer experience strongly preferred.
Experience supporting delegated healthcare models and healthcare operations.
Experience with Health Solutions Plus (HSP) and healthcare payer administration platforms highly preferred.
Experience participating in audits, regulatory reviews, RFP responses, and client-facing initiatives.
Experience with Agile delivery methodologies.
Familiarity with Azure, APIs, web portals, management information systems, and database technologies.
Experience collaborating with Scrum Masters and Project Managers.
Experience with DevOps practices and modern application delivery approaches.
Previous experience working with Conduent or similar healthcare technology partners is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

Successful candidates will be able to:

Build strong partnerships across business and technology teams.
Develop and retain engaged, high-performing employees.
Deliver reliable, secure, and business-focused technology solutions.
Balance competing priorities while maintaining operational excellence.
Drive innovation and modernization without losing focus on stability and service quality.
Lead with integrity, sound judgment, and a commitment to organizational success.

Why Join Liberty Dental Plan?

At Liberty Dental Plan, we believe our people are our greatest asset. We are committed to creating an environment where employees can grow professionally, contribute meaningfully, and make an impact. You'll join a collaborative organization where leadership is measured not only by results, but by the ability to develop talent, strengthen relationships, inspire innovation, and create lasting business value.

As the Director, IT Applications, you'll have the opportunity to influence enterprise technology strategy, lead meaningful transformation initiatives, mentor future leaders, and help advance solutions that support the health and well-being of the communities we serve.

Ready to make a lasting impact? Apply today and help shape the future of technology at Liberty Dental Plan.

Qualifications

Location

Our employees are distributed in office locations in multiple markets across the United States. We are unable to hire or allow employees to work outside of the United States.

What Liberty Offers

Happy, healthy employees enhance our ability to assist our members and contribute more actively to their communities. That’s why Liberty offers competitive and attractive benefit packages for our employees. We strive to care for employees in ways that promote wellness and productivity.

Our first-class benefits package supports employees and their dependents with:

Competitive pay structure and savings options to help you reach your financial goals.
Excellent 401(k) retirement benefits, including employer match, Roth IRA options, immediate vesting during the Safe Harbor period, and access to professional financial advice through Financial Engines.
Affordable medical insurance, with low-cost premiums for employee-only coverage. Liberty subsidizes the cost for eligible dependents enrolled in the plan.
100% employer-paid dental coverage for employees and eligible dependents.
Vision insurance with low-cost premiums for employee-only coverage and dependents.
Company-paid basic life and AD&D insurance, equal to one times your base salary, with options to purchase additional supplemental coverage.
Flexible Spending Accounts for healthcare and dependent care expenses.
Voluntary benefit programs, including accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurance.
Long-term disability coverage.
Expansive wellness programs, including company-wide wellness challenges, BurnAlong memberships, and gym discounts.
Employee Assistance Program (EAP) to support mental health and well-being.
Generous vacation and sick leave policies, with the ability to roll over unused time.
10 paid company holidays.
Tuition reimbursement for eligible educational expenses.
Remote or hybrid work options available for various positions.

Compensation

In the spirit of pay transparency, the base salary range for this position is $150,000 - $200,000 a year,
not including fringe benefits or potential bonuses. At Liberty, your final base salary will be determined by factors such as geographic location, skills, education, and experience. We are committed to pay equity and also consider the internal equity of our current team members when making final compensation decisions.

Please note that the range listed represents the full base salary range for this role. Typically, offers are not made at the top of the range to allow for future salary growth.

Liberty Dental Plan commits to maintaining a work environment that acknowledges all individuals within the workplace and will continue to engage in practices that are inclusive of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We strive to have every person within the organization have a sense of belonging while encouraging individuals to unleash their full potential. Liberty will leverage diverse perspectives in building high performance teams and organizational culture.

jobs.description:
NeighborWorks as a Company and an Employer

Picture yourself in a collaborative, diverse hybrid environment surrounded by colleagues who challenge, encourage and inspire you to support mission-driven work. This opportunity includes a competitive total rewards package with a 401(k) match of up to 12%, 11 paid holidays, generous leave (including 40 hours of paid volunteer time) and industry-leading benefits. Begin your career with NeighborWorks® America and gain access to our Staff Training and Education Program (STEP), designed to support your continued growth and development. For over 45 years, Neighborhood Reinvestment Corp., a national, nonpartisan nonprofit organization known as NeighborWorks America, has worked to make every community a place of opportunity. Our network includes nearly 250 organizations in every state, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico. NeighborWorks America provides grant funding, peer exchange, technical assistance, evaluation tools and professional learning as the nation's leading trainer of housing and community development professionals. NeighborWorks network organizations serve their communities with affordable homes—owned and rented—financial counseling and coaching, resident-led community building and partnerships in health, employment and education.

We hold ourselves and each other accountable.  

We act with integrity.  

We lead with curiosity.  

We pursue excellence with courage.  

We respect, honor and celebrate each other.  

We collaborate with purpose.  

Work at a Glance:
Strategic advisor on technology, cybersecurity, AI, and regulatory risk.

Reporting to the Chief Audit Executive, the Director Technology Risk Assurance leads the organization's technology risk assurance activities, including the identification and assessment of technology risk, cybersecurity, cloud, data governance, AI governance, and information assurance audit activities. The Director develops and executes a risk-based technology audit strategy and multi-year technology risk assurance roadmap that provides independent assurance regarding the effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal controls across the organization's technology environment.
The position serves as the primary subject matter expert for technology-related risks and provides strategic guidance to the Chief Audit Executive regarding cybersecurity, cloud computing, infrastructure, application controls, emerging technologies, artificial intelligence, and regulatory compliance. The Director leverages data analytics, continuous auditing techniques, and where feasible AI-enabled audit tools to improve audit efficiency and effectiveness while ensuring alignment with professional standards and leading frameworks including NIST, COBIT, COSO, AI governance frameworks, and IIA standards.

·     Evaluate the effectiveness of IT governance, cybersecurity, privacy, resilience, disaster recovery, cloud security, identity management, and technology risk management controls.
·     Assess compliance with applicable standards and frameworks including NIST, COBIT, COSO, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, and industry best practices.
·     Provide assurance over AI governance, responsible AI practices, model risk management, and compliance with emerging AI regulations and frameworks.

Lead outsourced and co-sourced technology internal audits.   Provide oversight, direction, and performance feedback to external consultants and audit resources assigned to technology assurance projects.

Stay current on emerging risks, evolving regulations, cybersecurity threats, AI developments, and leading audit practices. Champion the use of data analytics, automation, continuous auditing techniques, and AI-enabled tools to improve audit effectiveness and efficiency.
·     Perform other duties as assigned by the Chief Audit Executive.

As part of the audit work activities and internal relationship building, maintains close contacts with the corporate staff, Executive Senior Management, Officers and staff of the Audit Committee Chair, Information and Technology Service, External Auditors, and Third-Party Service Providers.

Data Analytics

If this kind of work and our kind of people energizes you, you’ve found the right place.

Who You Are

You’ve spent 10+ years in custom software consultancies, and you’ve been a regular presence on both sides of the business: in the room helping win the work, and in delivery helping build it. You know how to pitch a client honestly and then stand behind what you promised.

You’re highly articulate and commercially fluent. You can talk architecture with a skeptical engineering lead in one meeting and talk ROI with a client’s CEO in the next, and both walk away trusting you. You understand how technical choices shape whether a project makes money because you’ve had to make those calls yourself.

Your technical judgment comes from years of hands-on work, and you keep it current in two ways: you read widely, and you keep doing the work. “Doing” might be a few hours each week staying sharp with new tools, or it might be real delivery responsibility on a live engagement. Either way, you don’t run on knowledge that stopped accruing years ago.

You ask experienced technologists the kind of sharp questions that send them back to their desk thinking.
You know a good deal across a wide range of subjects and connect ideas others keep separate.
You’re an excellent communicator, in writing and on your feet.
You bring out people’s best work through interpersonal connection and high standards.

Your name carries some weight in the communities you’re part of. When you write or speak, senior engineers pay attention, and a few of them want to come work with you.

This is primarily a market-facing role. You’d rather be out in the market shaping where we go than waiting inside for an assignment.

Drive our go-to-market direction rather than wait for it. Bring a point of view and help us continuously iterate on where we should show up, what we should say, and which opportunities are worth chasing.

Internally, your footprint is lighter but real. You’re the standard other technologists measure themselves against, and you’re a mentor to those working on their business leadership and impact. You’ll weigh in from time to time on technical job standards and career pathing. You’ll start without direct reports and lead through influence, and as we grow, the role could grow into leading a small team.

A track record of pitching and winning enterprise engagements inside a consultancy

Relationships with cloud or AI platform partners, and the standing that comes with them

Some of the biggest names in the progressive space have leaned on us as their trusted IT + cybersecurity partner. We are looking for top IT talent as we continue to scale our team.

About the Role

Personified is looking for a Senior Vice President of Technology to run the operational core of our technology organization: engineering, client support, cybersecurity, and IT operations. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who has run these functions inside a managed service provider before and knows exactly what breaks at scale: ticket queues, on-call rotations, security posture, tooling debt, and how to fix it without slowing the team down.

You'll report to the CTO and own execution across four functional leaders and the day-to-day delivery. You are the person who makes sure the trains run on time, the team is accountable, and our 97% client retention rate stays exactly where it is, or gets better.

This role exists because Personified is growing past the point where one person can run every function directly. We need someone who has done this before, who can walk into a room of client support engineers or a security incident and immediately know what questions to ask.

Key Responsibilities

Client Support & Service Delivery
— Ensure the team hits our response-time and resolution standards across every client tier. Own escalation paths, staffing models, and the systems (like our Halo ticketing platform) that keep support predictable and measurable.

Engineering
— Oversee infrastructure, systems engineering, and technical delivery. Set standards for process discipline, documentation, and accountability across the engineering team.

Cybersecurity
— Own the operational security posture across our client base: monitoring, incident response, vulnerability management, and compliance readiness. Make sure security isn't a side conversation — it's built into how we operate.

IT Operations
— Drive the shift from manual, reactive IT operations toward automation and repeatable processes. Reduce the operational load on the team while improving consistency for clients.

People leadership
— Directly manage functional leaders across these four areas. Set clear expectations, run a real performance management cadence, and build a bench of leaders under you who can eventually run without your direct involvement.

Cross-functional operations
— Be the connective tissue between functions that too often operate in silos. When a client issue touches support, engineering, and security at once, you're the person who makes sure it gets resolved as one coordinated response, not three separate ones.

Metrics and accountability
— Build and own the operational scorecard for technology delivery: response times, resolution rates, security incidents, retention impact. Bring data, not anecdotes, to every conversation with the CTO.

Travel
or work or present onsite as needed to support business needs, ensure continuity of service, and represent Personified to our clients and partners at the highest level.

Skills + Experience

8+ years in technology operations leadership, with at least 4 in a managed service provider (MSP) environment, you understand ticket economics, SLAs, multi-client environments, and the specific pressure of supporting many organizations at once rather than one.

Direct people-management experience across multiple technical functions simultaneously (not just one discipline). You've managed managers, not just individual contributors.

A track record of taking an under-disciplined operation and making it measurably more consistent, without making it slower or more bureaucratic.

Real fluency in cybersecurity operations; you don't need to be the deepest technical expert in the room, but you need to know enough to ask sharp questions and hold a security leader accountable.

Experience building or scaling IT automation — you should be able to speak concretely about a time you replaced manual process with something repeatable.

A communication style that is direct and specific. You document decisions. You don't let vague problems stay vague.

What Would Make You a Great Fit Here

You've worked with or served mission-driven, nonprofit, or advocacy organizations before, and you understand why 'the client hired us so they never have to think about IT again' is a real design principle, not a slogan.

You're comfortable in a smaller, fast-moving company where your title doesn't insulate you from doing real work.

You believe good process makes teams faster, not slower, and you can tell the difference between bureaucracy and discipline.

You want to build a team, not just manage one that already exists.

Reporting Structure

This role has direct management authority over the functional leaders in Client Support, Engineering, Cybersecurity, and IT Operations. It reports to the CTO, who retains direct ownership of Technical Programs and Training/Content, along with technology strategy, senior-level accountability, and cross-company initiatives.

You’ve spent 10+ years in custom software consultancies, and you’ve been a regular presence on both sides of the business: in the room helping win the work, and in delivery helping build it. You know how to pitch a client honestly and then stand behind what you promised.

You ask experienced technologists the kind of sharp questions that send them back to their desk thinking.

new_jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Senior IT Project Manager
leads the design, development, and implementation of information systems across the full system development life cycle, from requirements through go-live and transition to operations. Supported systems may include Medicaid Management Information Systems (MMIS), eligibility and enrollment systems, enrollment broker platforms, learning management systems, web portals, and data and reporting solutions. This role manages multi-year federal, state, and corporate projects with budgets of $500,000 and higher.

This is a full-time position located in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the initiation, planning, execution, and closing of IT and professional services projects across the entire system development life cycle (SDLC), covering requirements, design, development, testing, deployment, and post-implementation support.
Serve as the primary liaison among the end client, vendors, stakeholders, and the hiring organization, managing communications and progress reporting to ensure project success, client satisfaction, and a positive team experience.
Define and develop project scope, deliverables, tasks, resource plans, schedule baselines, and expenses, while managing resource allocations and providing timely performance feedback.
Monitor project budgets and hours to meet target gross margin goals, accurately forecast resource utilization and revenue recognition, and review and approve client and subcontractor invoices.
Apply Waterfall, Agile/Scrum, or hybrid delivery methodologies based on client requirements, coordinating backlog, sprint, and release planning with product owners.
Facilitate requirements gathering and elicitation sessions, maintain a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM), and partner with business analysts, developers, solution architects, and quality assurance (QA) teams to translate business requirements into technical designs.
Identify, track, and mitigate project risks, including technical risks, system interfaces, integrations, and environment dependencies.
Ensure all project deliverables meet organization standards and client specifications, overseeing system, integration, and user acceptance testing (UAT), defect triage, and go/no-go readiness decisions.
Coordinate with third-party vendors, system integrators, and client IT organizations, and define statements of work (SOWs) for subcontract partners.
Support federal oversight activities as applicable, including Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) certification, Advance Planning Documents (APDs), and Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) reviews.
Collaborate with technical, organizational change management (OCM), and training teams to ensure end-user readiness for system launch.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, or Program/Project Management, or equivalent work experience.
Project Management Professional (PMP)® Certification.
At least 7 years of experience managing IT projects for external customers, including at least 5 years managing system implementations.
Demonstrated experience successfully managing IT projects exceeding $500,000 in budget.
Proven track record of delivering at least one large-scale system implementation from initial requirements through go-live.
Experience managing projects with federal government, state government, and private-sector clients.
Working knowledge of software development, system integration, APIs, and data flows sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams.
Ability to communicate technical issues clearly to non-technical executives and program staff.
Demonstrated consultative, conflict management, customer service, and negotiation skills to achieve mutually agreeable solutions.
Superior writing and verbal communication skills, along with strong organization, prioritization, and time management abilities under pressure and tight deadlines.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and collaborate effectively across diverse personalities and organizational levels.
Proficiency with project management and delivery tools, such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or ServiceNow.
Familiarity with cloud-based and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) implementations.
An AI-forward mindset with the ability to effectively and responsibly leverage AI tools and technologies to support project planning, documentation, analysis, communication, and overall daily project management activities.

Preferred Qualifications

Agile certification, such as PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP)®, Certified ScrumMaster® (CSM), or SAFe®.
Health and Human Services (HHS) or Medicaid systems experience (such as MMIS, eligibility and enrollment, enrollment broker, or data and reporting systems).

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

Regularly required to sit, stand, talk, hear, and utilize technology tools such as a laptop computer for extended periods.
Specific vision requirements include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.
Ability to occasionally lift up to 20 pounds.
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Description

Are you passionate about technology, engineering and operational excellence? Would you like to help Amazon customers meet their daily needs? If you answered yes, Amazon’s Worldwide Grocery Stores Tech (WWGST) organization is looking for a Technical Program Manager (TPM) like you.

At WWGST, we are solving a fundamental need for customers - food and nutrition. We serve millions of customers around the planet by making it easier to solve their grocery needs through multiple offerings that meet them where needed. Whether it’s online or in-person, multiple brands, or supporting omni-channel shopping missions, we want Amazon to be the go-to relationship.

In this role, you will drive key engineering initiatives for the Identity and Access Management (IAM) team including the development and execution of excellence goals, operational planning, security fortification and technical readiness. Each of these areas are critical to ensure we can reliably serve our customers while continuing to innovate on our portfolio of solutions. You will work across the WWGST organization in partnership with tech teams and leadership to ensure we can deliver on this promise.

This is a unique opportunity for someone interested in working in an entrepreneurial environment to drive deliverables with visibility and impact. The successful candidate will possess a strong program management background, have demonstrated experience leading large programs, and have a well-rounded technical background.

As a Technical Program Manager, you will be responsible for delivering programs with medium complexity and/or those that have broad cross-organizational, global, or technology impact. Your work will focus on large product, process and engineering efforts that solve complex problems. You will be trusted to operate with complete independence and are often assigned to focus on areas where the business and/or technical strategy has not yet been defined.

Key job responsibilities

Drive high priority, complex projects across many teams.
Work with business owners to define requirements.
Collaborate with tech teams on technical design.
Own the program execution and delivery process, including how to deliver iteratively, early and often.
Help resolve blockers to program delivery.
Proactively identify and mitigate project risks by anticipating challenges and taking ownership of outcomes.
Effectively partner with all levels of leadership.
Able to represent, verbally and in writing, complex decisions, trade-offs, and potential solutions clearly to leaders to help them understand the decisions they have to make and the options they have.
Influence organizational priorities, system owners, business, and technology direction.
Manage cross-functional communication to ensure all stakeholders are informed and needs aligned.
Recognize when current programs are susceptible to prior failure patterns and actively steer leadership to avoid repeating these failures.
Know when a design or solution requires additional technical guidance and seek their input.
Show excellent judgment in driving executive-level escalations.
Deliver solutions that meet Amazon high standards for customer satisfaction, efficiency, stability, extensibility, simplicity, and operational excellence.
Amplify your impact by educating the TPM and engineering communities (within your organization as well as more broadly) on program management best practices.
Participate, sharing knowledge and collaborating with other TPMs, specifically attending and/or presenting at internal conferences.

About The Team

WWGST's IAM Operational Excellence team's objective is to unify identity and security and integrate that unity into data, applications, & technology building blocks. We deliver an architecture that supports seamless authentication, fine-grained authorization and adaptive access control supporting modern, legacy applications and data consumption requirements. We simplify the service by providing the right access, to the right people, at the right time, for the right reason, at the right cost.

3+ years of technical product or program management experience
3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
2+ years of software development experience
Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in system design
Experience developing and executing/delivering product and technical roadmaps
